script:
In Japan, people collect sewer lids like rare trading cards.

After dark, a collector crouches under a streetlight, photographing a colorful lid instead of stealing it. Japan's decorated manholes are public infrastructure, but fans treat each local design like a rare release.

The hunt continues at a city office, where the same design appears on a manhole card. These cards are handed out locally, often one per person, so collectors travel to the place instead of ordering online.

Back home, cards go into plastic pages beside phone photos, dates, and locations. Serious collectors plan whole trips around covers, while the real lid stays outside, exactly where everyone walks over it.
